title: Your dApp is 90% Web2: Rebuilding One App on the Open Stack.
description:
Take a normal map app: places, reviews, photos. Press X-ray and you see what it quietly depends on: a server, a database, a bucket, an account system, a host, a domain, a code host and a CI pipeline. Each of these has taken real apps down: a datacenter fire, cloud and CDN outages, a code host removing a project, a poisoned npm package.

Then we rebuild it on stage, layer by layer. Login moves to a wallet, and the app is now hybrid, like most dApps. Then the data becomes Arkiv entities anyone can query, photos and map tiles move to Swarm, a wallet signs every write, and the app, its name, its source code and its build move to Web3 pieces. Each step is animated, explained and run live, until the X-ray shows 100% Web3.

We close with how it was built overnight by a team of AI coding agents: the prompts, the tools and the checks.
abstract: Most dApps are a Connect Wallet button on top of a Web2 stack. We take one app, a small Google Maps clone, and move it live from Web2 to hybrid to 100% Web3, one layer at a time, while the room adds places to the map from their phones. You leave knowing what every layer of your own app depends on and how to move it, plus the AI agent workflow that built it.
